title: KPT step 5: distinguish the families
summary: Combine only the four KPT families that were taught in separate blocks.
objectives: Choose which known family a supplied pair uses.
Keep KPT separate from the ending.
Prepare to use known weak stems in later noun, verb, and plural lessons.

sections.title: Ask one comparison question
paragraphs: Which consonant letters differ between the supplied first and second forms? Answering that question identifies the KPT family.
You are not expected to predict an unfamiliar word.

sections.title: The next lessons add endings
paragraphs: This mixed block still focuses on seeing the consonant change.
Later lessons will explicitly separate two construction steps: make the known weak stem, then add an ending.

steps: Ignore final -n when naming the KPT change.
Recognise this as a learned special-k pair.
Do not generalise it to every word with k.

commonMistakes: Do not choose a rule from the English meaning.
Do not treat an ending as part of KPT.
Return to the smaller lesson if one family is still unclear.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in pankki (“bank”) → pankin (“of the bank”)?

optionFeedback.kk → k: Correct. This is the double-consonant family.
optionFeedback.k → ∅: “k → ∅” does not show the required pattern. This is the double-consonant family.
optionFeedback.nk → ng: “nk → ng” does not show the required pattern. This is the double-consonant family.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in jalka (“foot or leg”) → jalan (“of the foot or leg”)?
practiceExercises.explanation: This is the common single-k disappearance pattern.

optionFeedback.k → ∅: Correct. This is the common single-k disappearance pattern.
optionFeedback.k → j: “k → j” does not show the required pattern. This is the common single-k disappearance pattern.
optionFeedback.kk → k: “kk → k” does not show the required pattern. This is the common single-k disappearance pattern.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in poika (“boy”) → pojan (“of the boy”)?
practiceExercises.explanation: This is a separately learned special-k pair.

optionFeedback.k → j: Correct. This is a separately learned special-k pair.
optionFeedback.k → v: “k → v” does not show the required pattern. This is a separately learned special-k pair.
optionFeedback.p → v: “p → v” does not show the required pattern. This is a separately learned special-k pair.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in kenkä (“shoe”) → kengän (“of the shoe”)?

optionFeedback.nk → ng: Correct. This is the consonant-cluster family.
optionFeedback.nt → nn: “nt → nn” does not show the required pattern. This is the consonant-cluster family.
optionFeedback.mp → mm: “mp → mm” does not show the required pattern. This is the consonant-cluster family.
